_readme: The other giraffes. Walk up to one and a prompt appears; press E (or tap TALK)
to hear them, and again for their next line.
Each has `stages`: what they say depending on how many of the glowing things
she's collected. The stage with the highest `from` she's reached is the one
they use, so they get more and more excited as she goes.
They're fond of her and they're glad she came. Keep that if you rewrite them.
`at` is where they stand: [x, y, z]. `outfit` is a list from OUTFITS in
js/giraffe.js: topHat, partyHat, beanie, sunHat, flowerCrown, glasses, shades,
scarf, bowTie, sweater, cape, backpack. `loop` is how wide a circle they
wander in — trimmed automatically if it would walk them into a wall.
Nobody agrees on what the glowing things are called. That's on purpose.

say: Oh! You must be Sarah. We have all been so looking forward to this.
Todd made this whole world for you. Built it with Claude, apparently — I don’t know what that is, but he was very pleased with himself.
He moved that little house four times. Four! Said it wasn’t right yet.
There are glowy ball things dotted about, if you fancy it. Take your time. You’re very welcome here.
You’ve been finding the glowy ball things! Good for you.
They say something rather nice happens if somebody gets all sixteen. Nobody’s ever managed it.
I’m not saying it should be you. I’m just saying it would be lovely if it were.
Nine! You’re past halfway, and you’ve barely been here an afternoon.
Marlow’s been telling everyone. He’s insufferable about it. He’s so proud.
Keep going, love. We’re all rooting for you.
Fourteen. Fourteen! I’ve had to sit down.
Whatever happens when you get them all — and something will — I want you to know we’re glad it’s you.
Go on. Finish it.
Morning! Lovely day. They’re all lovely here, but this one especially — you turned up.
You’ll see the shinies about. Little floating ones. Very pretty, quite hard to reach.
There’s an old story that whoever collects all sixteen sets everything right. Makes the world better somehow.
Bit vague, as stories go. But a nice one to have around.
How many shinies have you got now? Don’t be modest.
That’s brilliant. Genuinely. Nobody gets past two or three usually.
I’ll tell Pip. Pip’s been waiting by the creek all week in a hat.
I looked the old story up properly. It’s better than I remembered.
‘And one shall gather the sixteen, and the world shall be kinder for it.’ That’s the line.
Kinder! Isn’t that nice? I do hope it’s you. I think it’s you.
Fourteen. I’m telling everyone. I’ve already told everyone.
Whatever you become at the end of this, could you remember I was encouraging early?
Very early. From the meadow. That was me.
I’ve had this hat on for three days in case you turned up. Absolutely worth it.
Orbs? Are they orbs? Nobody will tell me what they’re actually called.
Bertrand has a name for them that’s eleven syllables long. I refuse to say it.
You’re glowing a bit! In a nice way! Like you’ve been somewhere warm.
That’s the orbs, that is. They like you.
Get all of them! I want to see what happens! Everyone does!
NINE. Sorry. Nine. I got excited.
Clementine cried in the woods when she heard. Happy crying. Mostly happy.
You’re going to do it, aren’t you. You’re actually going to do it.
Two left! TWO! I’ve put the hat back on!
If you become something magnificent at the end, will you still come by the creek?
…Okay. Okay good. That’s all I wanted.
Mind your step in the trees, it goes dim. Beautiful though, isn’t it.
We call them the Lanterns here. Capital L. It felt respectful.
The old ones said sixteen was a number worth finishing. They never said why. They just smiled about it.
You’re warmer than you were. I felt you coming before I saw you.
The Lanterns weren’t dropped, you know. Somebody put them out there. On purpose. For somebody.
I’ve always wondered who they were waiting for.
The moss is leaning towards you. Look at it. It’s never done that.
I think this wood has been waiting a very long time for somebody like you.
Don’t stop. Please don’t stop.
You’re nearly there and I can hardly stand it.
I made you a flower crown. It’s at my house. I’ll give it to you after.
Go on. Go and be whatever the story says you’ll be.
Ah. The sister. Genuinely delighted, and I do not say that lightly.
They are properly called the Spheres of Considerable Significance. I have said so for years.
Pip calls them ‘orbs’. Pip also eats bark. I rest my case.
You carry several of the Spheres already. It suits you. It really rather does.
The old text is quite clear: sixteen, and the branches bow. I maintain these branches.
I should be delighted to bow. I’ve practised.
Eleven. I have been composed about this for some time and I would like that noted.
You are eleven-sixteenths of something wonderful and you’re being terribly casual.
The view from up here is the finest in the world. He built it that way for you deliberately.
Two remain. I have laid out a small buffet. It may be premature.
When it’s done — and it will be done — I should like to serve in whatever comes after.
Something in parks. I’m very good with branches.
Hey. Cool cactus, right? I like to think we match.
Those floaty bois out there? There’s a whole thing about them. Sixteen and the world gets better, supposedly.
I don’t usually go in for destiny. For you I’ll make an exception.
Okay, you’ve got a proper glow on now. That’s not a look, that’s an achievement.
Six floaty bois. Ten to go. Not that I’m counting. I am completely counting.
Whole beach is talking about you. In a good way. Mostly Odie, and Odie is me.
Eleven. Eleven! I had to sit on a rock about it.
You know the best part? Nobody asked you to do this. You just started, and you kept going.
That’s the most giraffe thing I’ve ever heard and you’re not even from here.
You’re two away and the sky’s already looking at you funny.
Go get them. Seriously. I’ll hold the cactus.
…I can’t hold the cactus. It’s a cactus. I’ll be here.
You made it all the way up here! Not everyone does. Sit a moment, the clouds are soft.
We just call them the Sixteen. Naming them felt like putting on airs.
Whoever finishes them doesn’t stay quite the same, they say. Becomes something better.
Seven, and still climbing. You’ve got a stubbornness about you. I like it enormously.
The Sixteen were scattered up cliffs and over water on purpose. Somebody wanted it to be earned.
Not too hard, mind. Just hard enough to mean something.
Twelve. You’ve done in an afternoon what nobody’s managed in generations.
I don’t think you’re special because of the Sixteen. I think the Sixteen waited for somebody like you.
Four to go and every one of them is above me. Off you go.
One left. At the very top. You know exactly where it is.
We’ll all be watching. Not nervously — the other way.
Go on, love. We’ve been waiting a long time for a day this good.
You’re a long way up. Nobody comes this high without a reason.
I’ve stood here a long time. I know what you’re looking for, and I’m glad it’s you looking.
I won’t slow you down. That was never my part in it.
So it is you. After all this waiting it’s somebody’s sister, come to visit.
Eight. Halfway. Everyone below is talking about you and every word of it is kind.
That doesn’t happen often. I’d hold onto it.
The sky’s gone lovely since you started climbing. Did you notice?
The story never said the sixteen would make somebody powerful. It said they’d make somebody kind, and the rest would follow.
Nobody ever reads to the end of things. That’s the best bit.
One left, and it’s just up there, and it always was.
Whatever you turn into — we already liked you. That part’s finished. That part was easy.
Go on. Go and see what he made for you.
